about: Gaps already known in how Ibid reads this document, each with the reason it is accepted for now. See scripts/answer-key.mjs.

accepted.reason: the conversion merged this footnote into the one before it, and the pane's two notes differ only in their paragraph number, so the alignment attributes it to a neighbouring note instead of this one. accepted.detail: a notice, which detection does not read
accepted.reason: cited by where it was published rather than by a number of its own, and detection does not read an Official Journal reference, so the instrument is not reported at all. The largest single gap these keys show: in competition practice the Commission's own notices and guidelines are among the most-cited instruments there are, and every short form a document then uses for one has nothing to resolve against

accepted.identity: judgment C-395/96 P Compagnie maritime belge transports
accepted.reason: the footnote contradicts itself, and Ibid follows the identifier the court minted. It reads “Judgment of 10 July 2001, joined cases C-395/96 P and C-396/96 P, Compagnie maritime belge transports and Others, ECLI:EU:C:2001:393”: the case numbers and the name are Compagnie maritime belge, whose judgment of 16 March 2000 is EU:C:2000:132, while the date and the ECLI are those of the order in C-497/99 P Irish Sugar — the other case the body names at this footnote. An ECLI is the court's own name for a document and a CELEX derived from a case number is an inference, so the ECLI is retrieved and the document shown is the one it names. What is missing is the warning: the check that reports a footnote contradicting its own ECLI compares the date's year and the court's letter, and here both agree
